# `tagged-vbr-mono.mp3` Fixture Provenance

Generated: 2026-11-23

An original, synthetic test fixture for issue #770: 1.5 seconds of 44.1 kHz mono, a rising
frequency sweep with a slow tremolo and a little noise, so that a decoder that lands even one frame
off the requested position produces a different sample. The source audio is generated by FFmpeg's
`aevalsrc`; it is not copied from a recording and carries no third-party content claim.

It has the structure of an MP3 written by a text-to-speech service: variable bit rate (about
87 kb/s) from `libmp3lame`, an ID3v2.4 tag (FFmpeg's encoder tag) ahead of the audio, and a Xing
header whose LAME extension declares the encoder delay and padding. The demuxer trims that delay
(1105 frames), so the stream's first decoded frame is timed at 25 ms rather than zero.

The file was encoded locally with FFmpeg `n9.0.2` using its `libmp3lame` encoder. FFmpeg and LAME
are build tools for this fixture only; neither is a Bloom runtime dependency. The LAME encoder is
LGPL-licensed.

```text
ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error \
  -f lavfi -i 'aevalsrc=0.4*sin(2*PI*(200+900*t)*t)*(0.6+0.4*sin(2*PI*3*t))+0.08*(random(0)-0.5):s=44100:d=1.5' \
  -ac 1 -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 3 -map_metadata -1 tagged-vbr-mono.mp3
```

`random(0)` makes the noise differ between runs, so a regenerated file has other bytes; the tests
compare against FFmpeg's own decode of the committed file, not against fixed sample values.
